_schema._description: Production / retrieval drills keyed by chapter label. Three drills per chapter: typically one translate-to-Latin, one form-picker, one vocab. Students complete them in the Exercitatio tab; chapters lock until the student has visited a scene from that chapter.

_kinds.translate: English prompt -> pick the right Latin
_kinds.form: Latin sentence with a blank -> pick the correct form
_kinds.vocab: Latin word -> pick the right English meaning

_fields.promptLa: (form/vocab) Latin sentence or word being asked about

Capitulum I.promptEn: How would you say 'I am Oedipus, king of Thebes'?
Capitulum I.explain: ego sum = 'I am' (1st person singular of esse). 'rex Thebarum' = 'king of Thebes' (Thebarum is genitive plural).

Capitulum I.promptEn: Pick the correct verb form to mean 'troubles' (the subject is pestis, 'plague').
Capitulum I.explain: Pestis is 3rd person singular, so the verb is vexat ('it troubles'). vexant would be 'they trouble'.

Capitulum I.promptEn: How do you say 'I will find the truth'?
Capitulum I.explain: Future tense -iam ('I will find'). The perfect inveni means 'I have found', and invenio means 'I find'.

Capitulum II.explain: Vates = a prophet who speaks for the gods (like Tiresias). Pastor = shepherd, nuntius = messenger, regina = queen.

Capitulum II.promptEn: How do you say 'Apollo speaks' (in the present)?
Capitulum II.explain: dicit = present 3rd person singular. dixit is the perfect (he said). dico is 1st person (I say).

Capitulum II.promptEn: Pick the form that means 'sees' (Tiresias is the subject).
Capitulum II.explain: Tiresias is 3rd person singular, so videt ('he sees'). The form videbo means 'I will see'; videbam means 'I was seeing'.

Capitulum III.promptEn: How do you say 'You are the crime!'?
Capitulum III.explain: es = 'you are' (2nd person singular of esse). Sum is 1st person ('I am'); est is 3rd person ('he/she/it is').

options: do not seek / do not ask
Capitulum III.explain: noli + infinitive = negative command in Latin. quaerere = 'to seek / to ask'. Tiresias keeps warning: noli quaerere — don't go looking.

Capitulum III.promptEn: Pick the perfect-tense form (the king said it once in the past).
Capitulum III.explain: dixit = perfect tense (he said — completed past). dicit is present ('says now'). The -xit ending is a classic perfect form.

Capitulum IV.promptEn: How do you say 'the queen's chamber'?
Capitulum IV.explain: Genitive case shows possession: reginae = 'of the queen'. Word order is flexible but the genitive ending tells you whose chamber it is.
Matrimonium = marriage. The Latin root mater (mother) is in there. Oedipus accidentally enters into matrimonium with his own mother.

Capitulum IV.promptEn: Pick the perfect passive form meaning 'was killed'.
Capitulum IV.explain: Perfect passive = participle (necatus) + est. necavit = 'he killed' (active). necabit = 'he will kill' (future active).

Capitulum V.promptEn: How do you say 'Polybus is dead'?
Capitulum V.explain: mortuus est = 'has died / is dead'. Polybus is masculine, so the participle is mortuus (not mortua, which is feminine).
Nuntius = messenger. The Corinthian nuntius brings the news that Polybus is dead — and the news that he is not Oedipus's true father.
portavi = 'I carried' (perfect 1st sg, ending -avi). portavit is 3rd person ('he carried'); porto is present ('I carry').

Capitulum VI.promptEn: How do you say 'I saved a baby'?
Capitulum VI.explain: infantem (object — accusative singular) + servavi (perfect 1st sg, 'I saved'). 'infans' is the nominative subject form.
Pastor = shepherd. The pastor saved baby Oedipus on the mountain — and finally tells the king the whole truth in this chapter.

Capitulum VI.promptEn: Pick the right form of 'to be' for 'you ARE' (when the shepherd accuses Oedipus).
Capitulum VI.explain: es = 'you are' (2nd person singular). est = 'he/she/it is'; sum = 'I am'; sunt = 'they are'.

Capitulum VII.explain: Iudicium = judgement, the moment of reckoning. The king must judge himself in this chapter.

Capitulum VII.promptEn: How do you say 'I will go into exile'?
Capitulum VII.explain: Future tense ending -bo: exsulabo = 'I will go into exile'. exsulat is present ('he goes into exile'); exsulavi is perfect ('I went').

Capitulum VII.promptEn: Pick the form meaning 'judges' (the subject is rex).
Capitulum VII.explain: rex is 3rd person singular: iudicat ('he judges'). iudicas = 'you judge'; iudico = 'I judge'; iudicant = 'they judge'.

Capitulum VIII.promptEn: How do you say 'the story is complete'?
Capitulum VIII.explain: fabula (subject, nominative feminine) + completa (feminine perfect participle) + est. The participle agrees with the subject in gender, number and case.
Fatum = fate. The English word 'fate' comes from it. Fata vincunt — the fates conquer.
vincunt = 'they conquer' (3rd person plural). fata is plural ('the fates'), so the verb is plural. vincit = 'he/she/it conquers'.
